text: Agile methodology is a popular way of managing projects, especially in software development. Instead of planning everything at the start, teams work in short cycles called sprints, usually lasting two to four weeks. Each sprint focuses on delivering a small, working part of the product. This iterative development allows teams to improve their work based on feedback. Before each sprint, the team chooses user stories from the backlog — a list of features and tasks described from the user's point of view. Every day, team members hold short meetings called standups to share progress and discuss problems. Agile helps teams stay flexible, communicate well, and respond quickly to change.
